title: Steve Miller Band
dek: Four eras, a song desk, and the three names The Joker keeps borrowing. Listen outbound. The receipt stays in this browser.
honesty: Listening notes. Album years, song homes, and writing credits follow public discographies linked in sources. No lyric transcription. No chart table.

receipt.label: browser-local
receipt.note: The receipt records the era, song, and persona last opened in this browser. It is not sent to PointCast.

eras.title: San Francisco blues
eras.note: The band starts in San Francisco in 1966, under the longer name Steve Miller Blues Band. A Capitol contract in 1967 shortens it to the Steve Miller Band. Children of the Future, the debut, is recorded in February 1968 and released that June, with Boz Scaggs still in the group. Sailor follows in October 1968: Living in the U.S.A., and Miller’s version of Johnny “Guitar” Watson’s Gangster of Love. Brave New World arrives on June 16, 1969, the first album after Scaggs and Jim Peterman leave, with Ben Sidran on keyboards and Space Cowboy on the record. Your Saving Grace, Number 5, Rock Love, and Recall the Beginning...A Journey from Eden carry the blues band through 1972. Enter Maurice is on that last one. The hit that will quote all of this has not been written yet.

eras.title: The persona turn
eras.note: The Joker, the album, is released on October 19, 1973. The title song is the archive. It calls back the space cowboy, the gangster of love, and Maurice, and it carries the coined word pompatus, which Miller has traced to a mishearing of Vernon Green’s puppetutes in the Medallions’ The Letter. The writing credit is Steve Miller with Eddie Curtis and Ahmet Ertegun, a public sign that the tune leans on an older rhythm-and-blues song of the same name. Before this record the band is an FM story. After it, the character has a face.

eras.title: Eagle years
eras.note: Fly Like an Eagle is released in May 1976. Book of Dreams follows in May 1977. Miller produces both. The first holds the title song, Take the Money and Run, and Rock'n Me. The second holds Jet Airliner, Jungle Love, and Swingtown. Same stretch of work, two temperatures: a wide synthesizer horizon, and songs that move like traffic. The blues guitar never leaves. This is the peak the rest of the map is walking toward.

eras.title: Abracadabra and after
eras.note: Circle of Love comes in 1981. Abracadabra, the album, is released on June 15, 1982, and the title song is the one this desk keeps. The studio record then thins out: Italian X Rays in 1984, Living in the 20th Century in 1986, Wide River in 1993, a long gap, then the blues covers Bingo! in 2010 and Let Your Hair Down in 2011. In 2016 Steve Miller enters the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame as a solo artist. The band’s name and the man’s name have been sharing a marquee the whole time.

songs.title: The Joker
songs.note: A slow introduction that gathers names the band had already used. The space cowboy, the gangster of love, and Maurice are citations, not new costumes. The Curtis and Ertegun credits sit beside Miller’s, so the song wears its rhythm-and-blues debt in the publishing line.
songs.why: It is the hinge. The San Francisco albums are the memory. The eagle years assume you have already met this character.

songs.title: Fly Like an Eagle
songs.note: The title song sits just after a short Space Intro, and the two pieces are one door. Synthesizer, a patient pulse, and a lyric about time that the band lets breathe. Miller wrote it and produced the record.
songs.why: This is the sound people mean by the eagle years. The blues band is still in the guitar. The room has gotten wide.

songs.title: Jet Airliner
songs.note: Paul Pena wrote it. The Steve Miller Band’s record, Miller producing, is the one radio kept. It is a road song with a brighter engine than the eagle title track, built for a band that had just learned how big a chorus could be.
songs.why: Book of Dreams is the companion volume to Fly Like an Eagle. This is its traveling song, and the desk credits the writer, not only the hit.

listen.youtubeCredit: Universal Music Group via YouTube. Composer credit on the upload: Paul Pena.

songs.title: Take the Money and Run
songs.note: Miller’s two-minute caper. Billy Joe and Bobbie Sue are the names in the story. The track moves like a blotter told with a grin, guitar up front, no wasted bars.
songs.why: The eagle album is not only the slow horizon of the title song. The same record can sprint.

songs.title: Rock'n Me
songs.note: Also Miller, also that album. Three minutes, a bright guitar figure, and a shout that feels like the band stepping into the sun after the synth fog of the title track.
songs.why: If Fly Like an Eagle is the glide, this is the snap. Play them back to back and the 1976 record makes sense as two temperatures.

songs.title: Abracadabra
songs.note: The title song of the 1982 album. Tighter than the mid-seventies suites, more of a pop spell, with an official video the band still points at. Miller writes it and the record carries his name into a new decade.
songs.why: It is the later door. After the eagle years the catalog slows down, and this is the song that kept the marquee lit.

songs.title: Space Cowboy
songs.note: Miller and Ben Sidran, on the first album after Boz Scaggs and Jim Peterman leave. The song names a persona the band will still be using in 1973. Sidran is the new keyboard voice. The psychedelic blues band is already talking to its later self.
songs.why: Hear this before The Joker and the nickname stops sounding like a costume. The hit is quoting a deep cut.

listen.youtubeCredit: Search YouTube. This desk does not embed an unverified upload.

songs.title: Jungle Love
songs.note: Turner and Douglass wrote it, first for Dave Mason, who passed. Turner brought a demo to Miller. Douglass has said the band cut it in about half an hour on the last day of the Book of Dreams sessions, with Douglass on guitar. A whistle, a riff, and not much plot beyond that.
songs.why: A side-musician song that became one of the set-list locks. The eagle years are not only Miller’s pen.

listen.youtubeCredit: Search YouTube. This desk does not embed an unverified upload.

songs.title: Swingtown
songs.note: Miller and Chris McCarty. A night-drive pulse from the same album as Jet Airliner and Jungle Love, with Gary Mallaber on drums in that mid-seventies band. Less story than motion.
songs.why: It is the third temperature of Book of Dreams. The FM peak is not one mood.

personas.title: Space Cowboy
personas.blurb: A name from 1969, on Brave New World, written by Miller and Ben Sidran. Not a costume added for the hit. The Joker picks the name up four years later and wears it in public. On this desk the cowboy is the through-line: the early psychedelic blues band talking to the later radio band.

personas.title: Maurice
personas.blurb: Enter Maurice is a 1972 track on Recall the Beginning...A Journey from Eden. The Joker, a year later, answers it by name. The coined word pompatus rides with that answer. Miller has traced it to a mishearing of Vernon Green’s puppetutes in the Medallions’ The Letter. A private joke became the most quoted idea in the catalog. This board does not print the line.

personas.title: Gangster of Love
personas.blurb: Johnny “Guitar” Watson’s song, in Miller’s hands on Sailor in October 1968, while Boz Scaggs was still in the band. The Joker cites it the way it cites Space Cowboy: as an earlier self. The gangster is the blues-root mask. The space cowboy is the San Francisco mask. Maurice is the in-joke. One 1973 song keeps all three in circulation.

sources.title: Steve Miller Band
sources.supports: Formation in San Francisco in 1966, the Capitol-era name change, album sequence, Boz Scaggs years, 2016 Rock and Roll Hall of Fame induction as a solo artist.

sources.title: Steve Miller Band discography
sources.supports: Release dates for Children of the Future (June 1968), Sailor (October 1968), Brave New World (June 16, 1969), The Joker (October 19, 1973), Fly Like an Eagle (May 1976), Book of Dreams (May 1977), Abracadabra (June 15, 1982), and the later studio albums.

sources.title: The Joker (song)
sources.supports: October 1973 single, writing credit (Miller, Eddie Curtis, Ahmet Ertegun), and the song’s citations of Space Cowboy, Gangster of Love, and Enter Maurice. Pompatus as a mishearing of Vernon Green.

sources.title: Brave New World (album)
sources.supports: June 16, 1969 release, departure of Boz Scaggs and Jim Peterman, Ben Sidran on keyboards, Space Cowboy credited to Miller and Sidran.

sources.title: Jungle Love (song)
sources.supports: Book of Dreams, writers Lonnie Turner and Greg Douglass, the Dave Mason pass, and Douglass’s account of a last-day session.

sources.title: Book of Dreams (Discogs release notes)
sources.supports: Swingtown credited to Chris McCarty and Steve Miller. Jungle Love credited to Greg Douglass and Lonnie Turner. Gary Mallaber on drums.
